question.text: Per recent SEBI circular referenced in the chapter, a Category III AIF is NOT permitted to adopt which of the following models?

answer.text: Charging differential management fees across classes
Issuing different classes of units to other investors such as employees, sponsor and permitted investor groups
A 'priority distribution model' where one class of investors receives higher share of profits at the cost of another class
Disclosing separate Series NAV for each class

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'As per recent SEBI Circular, no Category III AIF can adopt such a priority distribution model, in which one class of investors are getting a higher share of profits, at the cost of another class of investors.' The wider AIF framework also states that no AIF scheme can adopt a priority distribution model. The Trap: Differential management fees, different classes of units (with separate NAV for those classes/series) are expressly contemplated by the workbook; only a priority distribution that favours one class at the cost of another is prohibited. Note: The ban targets the economic split between classes, not the existence of multiple classes, differential fees or class-wise NAV reporting.
